summary: Per-scene pack-resource handle table owned by Ui_SceneFlow (self+0x60): a PackHandle[26] slot array at +0x38 with a parallel 16-byte status record per slot at +0xa8, the mounted common 2D pack's object/handle pair at +0xa0/+0xa4, and three intrusive lists of objects to destroy or release.
evidence: 26-slot handle array at +0x38..+0x9f (Acquire writes 'table + index*4 + 0x38', ReleaseAll loops 0x1a handles from +0x38 and calls Pack_FreeHandleEntry); slot records at +0xa8 + index*0x10 (Acquire tests '+0xa8 + index*0x10', Add increments 'iVar6->f_a8' and writes 'iVar6->f_ac'); Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownAll passes the typed 'self->f_60' (Pack_HandleTable*) to Pack_HandleTable_ReleaseAll/ReleaseObjects. Caveat: Pack_HandleTable_Get (0x0010AF94, also listed under this class) actually builds the 0x2C64-byte named-object bucket cache used by Fs_NamedObject_GetOrCreate, so that one function probably belongs to a different class.

fields.name: maybe_listEndMarker
fields.evidence: Pack_HandleTable_ReleaseObjects: 'while (*piVar5 != *(int *)(param_1 + 0x14))' - the end marker of the first intrusive list, compared against each node's first word; the walk starts from +0x18

fields.name: maybe_listFirstNode

fields.name: maybe_list2FirstNode

fields.name: slot1PackHandle

fields.name: commonPackHandle

summary: Head of the multiple-inheritance object built by Pack_HandleEntry_Init: three base-subobject vtable pointers at +0/+4/+0xc/+0x14 with their zeroed state words, immediately followed by an inline array of twenty 0x28-byte sub-handles at +0x1c - the 24-byte size covers only the first subobjects.
evidence: Pack_HandleEntry_Init (0x001242AC) calls the base ctor at entry+4, stores 0x007824A4 at +0 and 0x007824A4+0x18 (secondary vtable) at +4, 0x00782234 at +0xc and +0x14 (two subobjects of the same base), zeroes +8/+0x10/+0x18, then std_ConstructArray(entry+0x1c, 0x28, 0x14) builds twenty 0x28-byte elements; the same ctor is called by Pack_HandleTable_Get and Pack_FreeHandleEntry, which then overwrite +0/+4 with their own vtables (0x00782A6C), so the recovered 'size' is only the head of a much larger allocation.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: 'piVar1[-1] = 0x007824A4;' with piVar1 = entry+4 stores the primary vtable; every caller replaces it with its own (Pack_HandleTable_Get: '*piVar3 = 0x00782A6C')

fields.name: secondaryVtable
fields.evidence: the same ctor stores 0x007824A4+0x18 here - a secondary vtable 0x18 bytes (6 slots) into the primary vtable, i.e. the second base subobject

fields.name: maybe_baseStateA
fields.evidence: 'piVar1[1] = 0;' clears the first data word of the base subobject whose vtable is at +4; no other read or write was recovered

fields.name: subVtableB
fields.evidence: 'piVar1[2] = 0x00782234;' - vtable of another base subobject at +0xc

fields.name: maybe_baseStateB
fields.evidence: 'piVar1[3] = 0;' clears the data word after the +0xc base vtable; no other access was recovered

fields.name: subVtableC
fields.evidence: 'piVar1[4] = iVar2;' with iVar2 == 0x00782234 - a second subobject using the same base vtable as +0xc

summary: 0x126c-byte Fs/pack resource entry object (the type accepted by Pack_AcquireResourceHandle) whose last member is a PackHandle at +0x1268; only its deleting destructor was recovered.
evidence: maybe_Pack_Entry_Dtor (0x005A5FD0): '*self = vtable; Pack_Handle_Dtor(self + 0x1268); ... operator delete', i.e. a 0x126c-byte object with a PackHandle as its final member; Pack_AcquireResourceHandle (0x006F0F5C) takes the same object as 'PackEntry*' and reads its part pointer (+0x58), part size (+0x5c) and format id (+0x60 == the part's +0x20) after checking its RTTI descriptor 0x007E7250; the caller is Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: '*self = vtable;' - the deleting destructor installs the class vtable at offset 0

fields.name: packHandle
fields.evidence: 'iVar1 = Pack_Handle_Dtor(param_1 + 0x49a);' - 0x49a u32-words == byte +0x1268, a 4-byte generation-tagged pack handle released through the global handle table 0x007BA2D0; 4716-4 == 4712 makes it the last member

summary: Non-deleting destructor slice of an Fs_Resource-derived object that owns four PackHandle members (+0x3c, +0x48, +0x54, +0x58) and switches back to the Fs_Resource base vtable 0x0077F6C4 while being destroyed; only its vtable and its last handle are attributed to this class.
evidence: maybe_Fs_Resource_DerivedDtor (0x0061D288, R3_020) is 'Pack_ReleaseHandle(self + 0x16)' (0x16 u32-words == byte +0x58), then the same call on +0x54 and +0x48, a store of the base vtable 0x0077F6C4 at +0, and one more on +0x3c, returning the base; R3_020 recorded it as byte-identical to the destructor inlined into Gfx_SceneSpritePool_Dtor (0x00620A78); the batch's class name comes from the recovered type name, the code is a D1 of an Fs_Resource-derived class.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: the destructor stores the incoming derived vtable at +0 and later restores the Fs_Resource base vtable 0x0077F6C4 at the same address

fields.name: packHandle
fields.evidence: 'iVar1 = Pack_ReleaseHandle(param_1 + 0x16);' - 0x16 u32-words == byte +0x58; the dtor releases four handle members (+0x58, +0x54, +0x48, +0x3c) and 0x58+4 == 92 == the class size, so this is the last one
